summary: Regression archaeology across 126 Downloads zips, six Netlify deploys (A-F), the real Jun 12-13 source trees and the abandoned code-split lineage. Key conclusions: (1) Netlify deploy IDs are ObjectIds; decoded, the live deploy 6aa16d61 was created Sep 9 2026 10:29:53 EDT (Sep 29 is only the download date) and nothing has been deployed since, so the Sep 18/26 RUM spikes are not code; the three grey RUM bands at Sep 7-9 most likely equal an un-downloaded deploy plus E (Sep 8 16:05) and F (Sep 9 10:29). (2) The main JS (index-Cg8FAMXN.js md5 7ef75b95) has been byte-identical since Jul 29 and in every deploy C-F; data files are byte-identical since Jun 12; so every bundle bug predates the RUM window and September changes are index.html/SW/site-nav/netlify.toml/sub-pages only. (3) Oldest bugs are day-one: date +2 at 4 sites in the first source; setGoldUnit/clearGoldTrail/drawGoldTrailSegment unbound since gettysburg_FIXED_circular (Jun 13 13:57) and the whole gold-trail engine is absent from the bundle (108 days live). (4) C3/C4 is a partial-fix artifact: v10 (Jun 13 18:49) re-based only the toolbar clock to 6:00/4:00, v20 (Jun 16 10:48) fixed only that function's date; chronology labels fit the 5:00 formula for 43/137 events and the toolbar clock for 2/137; the data schema itself says Day 2 = 5:00am-7:50pm in 225 ticks. (5) C1/C2 were born with the mobile layout (v16 Jun 16 09:55, Tools sheet v26 11:31, credit row v28 13:46): App renders desktop Timeline/header/Sound unconditionally at equal z-index 100. (6) C6: SW registration first appears in E, controllerchange reload in F; Lighthouse trace shows two Document requests (t=1 and 909 ms), 37 data URLs fetched twice, redirect audit 9,070 ms vs simulated mobile LCP 9,007 ms while observed LCP is 287 ms, so the mobile lab failure is mostly the reload artifact. (7) C8 is E's span-to-button conversion without a background reset (D was fine). (8) The 'content hash' name is reused for >=40 different byte-contents under immutable caching and SW cache-first. (9) No earlier deploy is a better base; best interim is F minus its three F-only additions (reload, extra h1s, Monuments hack) via index.html hotfix. (10) Lost goods: code-splitting (276 KB / 6 KB entry / 100 KB entry builds), real 65-file source + 63-check validator + CI, lineage-Y features (Night Mode, Distance panel with units+march time, Find Location, unit history), GSC verification file, a working enforcing CSP (Jun 22), A's canvas Distance line. (11) Secrets: no private keys; Mapbox token #1 in deploy A/older bundles and .env.local files is revoked, token #2 valid; Google Maps Embed key in bundle since Jun 16; old deploy permalinks and the netlify.app host still serve landing.html (pricing), diagnostics.html and the full site. 34 fix-spec findings follow; full evidence, per-issue introduced-in table, timeline, and rollback matrix are in the report.

findings.title: Content-hash every asset; stop reusing index-Cg8FAMXN.js for different bytes; generate the SW precache list from the manifest
findings.evidence: index-Cg8FAMXN.js is the filename of >=40 distinct byte-contents across 62 zips from v29 (Jun 16 13:50) to Sep 6 (zipscan.py). Deploy B md5 0903f96b (2,280,095 B) vs C-F md5 7ef75b95 (2,280,438 B) under the same name. netlify.toml /assets/* is 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable' (B:23, F:23). F sw.js:41-47 is cache-first for every /assets/* request and F sw.js:5-13 hardcodes '/assets/index-Cg8FAMXN.js' in PRECACHE_ASSETS with a manual CACHE_NAME ('gbg-v5', line 3). F index.html:259-263 comment: deploy changes 'silently don't show up until a hard refresh'.
findings.root_cause: The deployed app is hand-patched minified output (no source); the filename is kept so index.html and sw.js need no edit, which defeats content-hash cache busting and makes browsers/SW serve stale JS. F's reload-on-controllerchange hack is a band-aid over this.
findings.fix: Add scripts/release.mjs run before every deploy: (1) for each file in assets/ compute sha256, rename to <name>-<hash8>.<ext>, rewrite references in index.html (modulepreload + script tag + css), inside JS chunks (dynamic imports './HelpModal-CFV9T0zH.js', './BookmarkPanel-C5YT4b5k.js', worker URL) and in sw.js; (2) write dist/asset-manifest.json and have sw.js precache only entries from it (no hand-edited list); (3) add a CI/pre-deploy guard that downloads the currently published deploy's asset list and fails when any filename exists with different bytes; (4) keep Cache-Control immutable only for hashed names; (5) until the pipeline exists, every manual patch must rename the file (sha8) and update index.html and sw.js in the same commit.
findings.acceptance_test: For every file in assets/, basename hash == sha256(file)[:8]. Guard script: 'compare published deploy vs candidate' exits non-zero if a same-name file differs. After deploying a patched bundle, a browser holding the previous deploy loads the new JS on the next plain navigation (Playwright: visit old deploy permalink, then new deploy, assert new bundle URL requested).
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Reliability (stale JS), repeat-visit performance, removes root cause of C6 workaround; prerequisite for any SW/precache strategy
findings.correction: Name reuse reproduced (45 distinct md5 across 86 of 189 zips vs >=40 claimed); sw.js:5-13/41-47, netlify.toml:23, index.html:259-263 ok. Hash in dependency order (chunks, entry, then index.html/sw.js). InterpolationWorker-UfIWA2-E.js (672 B) is an orphan with no referrer, so the worker-URL rewrite is moot; delete the file.

findings.title: Hotfix C6: delete the controllerchange location.reload() and reg.update() hack from index.html
findings.evidence: f_sep09cur/index.html:258-272: 'var gtbgReloadedForSW=false; navigator.serviceWorker.addEventListener("controllerchange", ... location.reload())' plus 'register(...).then(reg=>reg.update())'. First appears in F (deploy 6aa16d61, Sep 9 10:29 EDT); E (Sep 8) registered the SW without the reload; the Jun 13 launch-day bundle stripped SW registration at 14:41. sw.js install calls skipWaiting() (line 17) and activate calls clients.claim() (line 30), so first install fires controllerchange for every first-time visitor. Only reload path in the site (bundle has none). Lighthouse lh_mobile.json: Document requests at t=1 ms and t=909 ms; 37 distinct /data URLs requested 76 times; redirects audit 9,070 ms; simulated LCP 9,007 ms vs observed LCP 287 ms.
findings.root_cause: controllerchange reload added to make deploys show without hard refresh (symptom of DH-01); clients.claim() on first install turns it into a guaranteed second page load for every new visitor and a mid-session reload on every SW update.
findings.fix: In index.html delete lines 259-268 (gtbgReloadedForSW + controllerchange listener) and change register call to 'navigator.serviceWorker.register("/sw.js").catch(function(err){console.warn("SW registration failed:",err)})' (drop reg.update()). Either also remove clients.claim() from sw.js activate (page becomes controlled on next navigation) or ship the kill-switch in DH-03. No automatic reload anywhere; if an update prompt is wanted, show a non-blocking 'New version available - Reload' button that calls reg.waiting.postMessage('SKIP_WAITING') and reloads only on click.
findings.acceptance_test: Playwright cold-profile visit to / for 15 s: exactly one framenavigated to '/' and one document request; requests to /data/*.json == 37 (not 76). Lighthouse mobile+desktop: 'redirects' audit passes; 'performance.getEntriesByType("navigation").length === 1'.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Mobile Lighthouse perf 64 -> expected >=85 (FCP 4.1 s and LCP 9.0 s lab values are dominated by the reload), desktop 85 -> 95+; RUM FCP/LCP for first-time visitors; Netlify pageviews stop being double-counted
findings.correction: Code and Lighthouse facts reproduce (Document requests at 0.63 ms and 908.8 ms, 37/76 data fetches, redirects 9,066.6 ms, observed FCP=LCP 287 ms; no other location.reload in bundle). Impact on simulated LCP is a hypothesis; see DH-26.

findings.title: Service worker: ship a self-unregistering kill-switch now, then a guarded SW with user-initiated updates
findings.evidence: History: SW registration existed in the Jun 13 14:31 bundle (FIXED_FINAL), sw.js became a 407-byte kill-switch at 14:37 (USEREF_FIXED) and registration was stripped at 14:41 (FINAL_v2). B-D shipped a caching sw.js that was never registered; E (Sep 8) registered it. F sw.js:41-47: cache-first for /assets/* with cache.put(e.request, clone) and NO res.ok guard (a transient 404/5xx during a deploy is cached and served forever until CACHE_NAME changes); sw.js:5-13 hardcodes hashed names so a rebuild with a new name makes cache.addAll reject and the SW stop updating; /data/ handler (61-68) also caches every response.
findings.root_cause: SW written for static hashed assets but paired with patched same-name assets and no build step; no update UX.
findings.fix: Interim (S): replace sw.js with 'self.addEventListener("install",()=>self.skipWaiting()); self.addEventListener("activate",e=>e.waitUntil((async()=>{for(const k of await caches.keys())await caches.delete(k);await self.registration.unregister();})()));' (do NOT navigate clients) and remove the register call from index.html, or keep registration but with no fetch handler. Target (M, after DH-01): Workbox injectManifest or hand-written SW that precaches asset-manifest.json entries with cache.addAll(urls.map(u=>new Request(u,{cache:'reload'}))), caches only responses where res.ok && res.type==='basic', network-first for HTML and /data/, versioned data URLs, message-based SKIP_WAITING, no clients.claim() on first install.
findings.acceptance_test: Interim: after deploy, navigator.serviceWorker.getRegistrations() returns [] on a browser that had the E/F SW after one more page load and caches.keys() is empty. Target: DevTools offline test loads app shell; forced 404 on one asset during install does not populate cache; two sequential deploys update without any auto-reload.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Reliability, repeat-visit LCP/FCP, removes P5 cross-world warnings source
findings.correction: Jun 13 SW timeline verified from zips (FIXED_FINAL 14:31 sw 4,060 B with 3 serviceWorker refs; USEREF_FIXED 14:37 sw 407 B; FINAL_v2 14:41 refs 0). A's 407 B sw is pass-through plus clients.claim(), not self-unregistering; the proposed unregistering interim SW is correct.

findings.title: C4: define one tick-to-clock/date model shared by the app and all sub-pages, and reconcile chronology labels/schema
findings.evidence: Formulas in play: (1) getTickTime bundle.pretty.js:9371-9382 start 6:00 Day 1, 4:00 Days 2-3 (introduced v10 Jun 13 18:49: '5*60' -> '(R===1?6*60:4*60)'); (2) JF :100837 and QF :100996 start 5:00; (3) compare.html:120 approxTimeForTick and living-ledger.html:135 timeForTick start 5:00 (living-ledger date +1 correct); (4) sandbox.html:104-105 hand-written 'mid-afternoon (tick 260)', '~3:00pm (tick 553)'; (5) documentary text '~7:30' at tick 12. chronofit.py on data/chronology_day1-3.json (unchanged since Jun 12): only 43/137 event labels equal 5:00+5min*(tick-dayStart); 2/137 equal the toolbar clock; Day 2 drift up to -230 min (tick 450 '7:50pm' vs formula 11:45pm), Day 3 median -70 min. data/placement_schema.json metadata.ticks_per_day says Day 1 '5:00am to 12:40am', Day 2 '5:00am to 7:50pm', Day 3 '5:00am to 8:05pm' (225 ticks each) which contradicts every uniform 5-minute formula. Anchor: tick 267 'Vincent arrives 8:25am' vs ~4:30pm historically.
findings.root_cause: No single time model was ever defined; the chronology was authored with labels that do not follow the tick grid, then partially 'fixed' in one function.
findings.fix: 1) Decide the model: (a) keep ticks as narrative order and derive labels via per-day piecewise scale from schema spans (Day1 1180 min/224 = 5.27, Day2 890/224 = 3.97, Day3 905/224 = 4.04 min per tick starting 05:00), or (b) re-key each event/placement tick from a historian-reviewed table of real clock times (needed for historical accuracy; e.g. Vincent 4:30pm -> tick ~400 on a 3.97 min grid). 2) Implement src/time.js exporting tickToClock(tick), tickToDate(tick), clockToTick(); import it in App/PlaybackStatus/FollowAncestor/MonumentSystem/Timeline/EventPanel and publish it as /assets/time-<hash>.js for compare/living-ledger/sandbox/documentary. 3) Regenerate all 137 chronology 'time' labels and vignette clock text from the model (script + reviewer sign-off list). 4) Delete the four private formulas.
findings.acceptance_test: Test: for all 137 events abs(parse(event.time) - tickToClock(event.tick)) <= 5 min; Playwright: same tick shows the identical clock string in toolbar, header, unit tooltip, Compare, Living Ledger, Sandbox labels, Documentary; historian sign-off checklist for 24 anchor events (first shot, Reynolds KIA, Vincent, Pickett step-off, etc.).
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Historical/data consistency C- -> A; Core function; credibility
findings.correction: Numbers reproduce (43/137, 2/137, drift). QF head is bundle.pretty.js:100998 with the 5:00 line at :101002, not :100996. Option (a) piecewise scale does not reproduce existing labels (Day 2 labels are 5-min-exact for early ticks 34/49 then compress; tick 267 at 3.97 min/tick = 7:43am vs label 8:25am), so it is a full relabel needing historian sign-off. The ~7:30 text is vignette data (vignettes_part1.json:32), not documentary.html.

findings.title: C5: restore the missing gold-trail engine, bind the three unbound identifiers, and make activateAncestor fail-safe
findings.evidence: Source FollowAncestor.jsx:15 (gettysburg_FIXED_circular, Jun 13 13:57; identical in v2_fixed) is 'export { initGoldCanvas, setGoldUnit, getGoldUnitId, drawGoldTrailSegment, clearGoldTrail } from ../engine/GoldTrailEngine.js' - a re-export does not create local bindings - but lines 103/104/115/204 call setGoldUnit/clearGoldTrail/drawGoldTrailSegment. Deployed bundle.pretty.js:101086 '(l(it), setGoldUnit(it), clearGoldTrail());' throws ReferenceError before flyTo/selectUnit run (101093-101111); :101101 drawGoldTrailSegment, :101229 setGoldUnit(null). bundle has 0 references to initGoldCanvas/getGoldUnitId/goldCanvas (grep) - the engine (GoldTrailEngine.js 1,442 B, MapView.jsx:66 init, AnimationEngine.js:117-122 per-frame draw) is tree-shaken out entirely. findings.fix: Minimal (M): (1) paste GoldTrailEngine.js content into the bundle scope as function declarations (setGoldUnit, getGoldUnitId, drawGoldTrailSegment, clearGoldTrail, initGoldCanvas) so the three bare identifiers resolve; (2) call initGoldCanvas(mapContainer) when the map loads (where the desktop map component gF mounts) and in the mobile map pO load handler; (3) in the animation frame function draw the gold segment for getGoldUnitId() as in AnimationEngine.js:117-122; (4) wrap the first statements of activateAncestor in try/finally so flyTo, selectedUnitId and currentTick=1 still run if the trail fails. findings.correction: Root cause confirmed (unbound identifiers at 101086/101101/101229; no definitions anywhere in DEPLOY_DIR; engine tree-shaken). The fix is wrong: st() (:101081-101111) projects segments before flyTo onto a screen-space canvas sized once, so the restored trail is misplaced after fly-to/pan/zoom. Use a lng/lat GeoJSON line layer updated via setData (like GtbgDist) and wrap trail calls in try/catch so flyTo/select always run. Effort M-L.

findings.acceptance_test: Lighthouse mobile LCP <= 2.5 s, FCP <= 1.8 s, TBT <= 200 ms, perf >= 95 (5 runs median); desktop perf >= 95; RUM p75 LCP <= 2.5 s over 7 days.
findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Lighthouse perf mobile 64 -> 95, RUM LCP/FCP Poor -> Good

findings.title: Replace the CSS preload + onload swap that produces 'preload not used' warnings
findings.evidence: C onward (c_aug22cur/index.html:43-45; F:56-58): '<link rel="preload" as="style" href="/assets/index-B4G7Z_2G.css" crossorigin onload="this.onload=null;this.rel=\'stylesheet\'">' with the real <link rel=stylesheet> deleted (B had both) and a <noscript> fallback. findings.fix: Use a plain '<link rel="stylesheet" href="/assets/index-<hash>.css">' (small) or inline critical CSS and load the mapbox stylesheet with rel=stylesheet media=print onload swap without preload; drop crossorigin for same-origin CSS; verify no console warnings in fresh and SW-controlled sessions.

findings.metric_or_grade_moved: Reliability/console cleanliness, Best Practices

verification_summary:
Most of the deploy-history evidence reproduces: line numbers, minified offsets, byte counts, deploy-ID decoding and the live curls all check out. Of 34 findings, 19 are confirmed, 13 corrected, 2 unverifiable and none refuted outright. The corrections mostly hit proposed fixes that would misfire:
- DH-06: the restored gold-trail canvas would be misaligned after flyTo.
- DH-08: root cause is incomplete; the site-nav.css button reset (color:inherit) overrides page colors.
- DH-18: the proposed CSP would break Watch Together (cdn.jsdelivr.net omitted).
- DH-20: adding defer to the Mapbox script breaks every map page.
- DH-28: the swap alternative conflicts with an enforced CSP.
- DH-30: the "lost" distance panel is not lost; the deployed one already shows ft/yd/m and march time.
- DH-13/24: "icons fixed in E" is wrong; the icons are still ~23% transparent and marked maskable.
- DH-14: the 500 KB gz initial-JS budget is unattainable with mapbox-gl in the initial payload.
- DH-02/26: the claim that the reload dominates the mobile LCP/FCP is a hypothesis, and Lighthouse's own document-latency-insight says no redirects.
A "## Verification" section with the full table, prose corrections and 8 missed issues was appended to deploy-history.md.
